messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed ~12% throughput regression on 8x A100 multi-GPU runs after the kernel-selector change landed yesterday. Same model/config that used to be stable.

alex: Repro'd on staging (model=rwd-small, seq=1024, batch=4/device). Confirmed lower tokens/sec and higher tail latency.

dina: I ran an nsys trace: `nsys profile -o /tmp/1748881234.nsys --trace=cuda,nvtx,nccl ./ci/run_inference.sh` — timeline looks weird, lots of small memcpy spikes before collective ops. Perfetto upload: https://perfetto.dev/trace/xyz (private).

infra-bot: Profiling artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-profiles/eng-runtime/1748881234/run.nsys (expires in 7d) :white_check_mark:

alex: From the timeline: repeated Host->Device memcpy right before every AllReduce, and many kernel launches on stream 1 while NCCL waits on stream 0. Hard to overlap. Snippet: 
```
Host->Device memcpy  18.9ms
kernel: query_kv     3.1ms
kernel: fused_gemm   2.0ms
NCCL AllReduce      11.7ms (idle wait)
```

maria: The kernel_selector update (v2.3) changed the matmul path chooser to prefer cuBLAS fp32 when seq<2048 to avoid a rare numerical edge-case. But nvprof counters show tensor-core utilization dropped — sm_efficiency down from ~72% to ~58% on the hot matmul.

dina: Also seeing KV cache handshake behavior: kv_prefetcher now uses pinned host staging buffers before async memcpy->device. That seems to add ~6–9ms extra per step on large-kv slices, because we end up serializing copies.

tim: I instrumented micro-benchmarks: isolating matmul vs gemm path shows cuBLAS fp32 path has higher latency for our GEMM dims and kills overlap with NCCL due to stream scheduling differences.

alex: Repro command I used: `python -m experiments.stress --model rwd-small --devices 8 --seq 1024 --batch 4 --profile nsys` — drop-in for someone to re-run.

maria: Proposed immediate mitigation: revert pinned-host staging in kv_prefetcher (use device-resident slices or cudaHostUnregister pattern) and tweak kernel_selector to fall back to the fp16/tensorcore path for these shapes. Also make NCCL launches on a dedicated stream and ensure kernel launches use non-blocking streams.

dina: I'll collect perf counters with nvprof for the failing shape: `nvprof --metrics sm_efficiency,gld_efficiency,gst_efficiency,dram_utilization -- ./ci/run_inference.sh` and attach results. Please also run a perfetto capture with sampling enabled (`nsys --sample=pc`).

alex: Building a tiny probe for allreduce overlap: `scripts/mg_allreduce_probe.py` — it runs the same kernels and prints per-step timings plus NCCL event gaps. Sharing output: 
```
step 0: compute 5.3ms, memcpy 19.1ms, allreduce wait 12.3ms
step 1: compute 5.2ms, memcpy 18.8ms, allreduce wait 12.6ms
```
This matches the trace (memcpy blocking).

infra-bot: Created issue INF-7123: "regression: multi-gpu memcpy+kernel scheduling causing NCCL overlap loss". Attached traces and nvprof dumps. Assignees: alex, dina.

maria: Assigning @alex and @dina as owners. Next steps: alex to land kernel_selector tweak (canary), dina to run nvprof/nsys counters and validate revert of pinned staging. Meeting 13:00 today to review perfetto. :calendar:

alex: I'll try the canary with two variants today: (A) force tensorcore fp16 path, (B) revert pinned host staging. Will post micro-benchmarks here. :eyes:

dina: If we confirm it's the staging + stream ordering, after the canary we should add a regression test that runs mg_allreduce_probe in CI nightly for 8-GPU to catch this.

maria: thanks — appreciate quick turnaround.
